conviction_note: The baseline has no reaction base rate at all, so I rebuilt what I could: the only two CXM prints I can date-and-price reliably both faded (Q1 FY27 on 2026-06-04 fell ~3.8% on soft guidance despite a beat; Q4 FY26 on 2026-03-11 gapped +9.4% pre-market and gave it back over the next two sessions), and 20d realised vol of 39.3% puts a normal CXM earnings session at roughly 4-8% absolute; I centre at -3.2 because the three things I found (a mechanical Citibank ASR bid whose scheduled termination date is 2026-09-01, the reported quarter having been run with no Chief Revenue Officer for two of its three months, and a Gulf war that re-escalated inside the quarter and again on 2026-08-31) all point the same way into a stock that has added 54% since 1 July and now trades above the 9-analyst average target, while the offsets (short interest 14-20% of float, $75m of buyback authorisation still live, ~4m shares coming back at ASR settlement) are real enough to keep the upper end of my band positive.

findings.finding: Sprinklr's $125m accelerated share repurchase with Citibank has a stated scheduled termination date of September 1, 2026 - the last session before the print - so the dealer's programmatic buying of roughly 21m shares (about 6-7% of the 2.76m-share ADV every day since 11 March) ends exactly as the event begins; the stock's 54% advance from $5.32 on 1 July to $8.21 on 31 August came in near-daily 1-3% increments with no news gap, and CXM was quoted down 3.3% at $7.94 on 2026-09-01 itself, the ASR's termination date.
findings.why_not_priced: The termination date lives in one sentence of a Q1 10-Q footnote ('The scheduled termination date is September 1, 2026 ... As of April 30, 2026, the ASR Agreement remained unsettled') and appears in no wire story, no preview and no analyst note; if the market had priced the withdrawal of the bid you would not see a 9-analyst average target of $7.88 sitting BELOW a $8.00 spot with nobody having refreshed since June, and you would not see the run-up delivered as a gapless daily grind - a fundamental re-rating on the Ribas board seat (17 Aug) or the Summer '26 release (15 Jul) would have produced a step, and in any case the run began on 1 July, weeks before both.
findings.independence: Independent price-history corroboration of the gapless grind and of the 2026-09-01 reversal: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/cxm/history/ (retrieved 2026-09-01, daily closes 1 Jul $5.32 through 31 Aug $8.21). Note this finding and the Ribas finding below both bear on 'the run-up has no fundamental basis', but they rest on different documents (the Q1 10-Q vs the 13 Aug 8-K).

findings.finding: The quarter being reported (1 May - 31 July 2026) was run without a Chief Revenue Officer for two of its three months: Scott Millard resigned effective 2025-11-11 after roughly seven weeks in the job, Tom Addis did not start until 2026-07-01, and SVP Global Sales Kevin Connolly left for NewRocket in the same window - so tomorrow's Q3 guide is the first ever set by a revenue chief with two months of tenure.
findings.why_not_priced: Each leg was reported once, months apart and framed positively (the 1 July 8-K exhibit quotes CEO Rory Read on Addis helping 'evolve our go-to-market model and accelerate into our next phase of growth'), and nobody has joined them into 'this quarter had no sales leadership'. If the market had priced an eight-month CRO vacancy across the seasonally-important Q2 you would expect the stock to be discounting the guide rather than trading 7.5% off its 52-week high with only three EPS estimates and a Hold consensus; a stock that had priced sales-execution risk does not add 54% into the print.
findings.independence: Separate source for the departure itself and the effective date: https://www.investing.com/news/sec-filings/sprinklr-chief-revenue-officer-scott-millard-to-depart-company-93CH-4351009 (2025-11-12, matching 8-K accession 0001193125-25-275969 filed 2025-11-12). Addis start date independently in the company's own 8-K exhibit: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001569345/000119312526291553/d106582dex991.htm (2026-07-01).

findings.finding: The Iran-Gulf war, which Sprinklr's 10-Q says caused 'inaccessibility, and potential loss, of certain customer data' at a third-party UAE data centre and which management sized on 4 June as $3-4m of slipped deals plus 54 customers force-migrated to Ireland, escalated again INSIDE the reported quarter (Iranian missiles and drones fired at Gulf states on 2026-07-12) and hostilities resumed on 2026-08-31 - against a guide that assumed 'improvements in the coming quarters', with 44% of FY26 revenue generated outside the Americas.
findings.why_not_priced: The March 1 AWS me-central-1 strike and its Q2 cost were disclosed and guided for on 4 June and are priced; the July 12 re-escalation and the 31 August resumption both post-date the guide, and with three EPS estimates on the name there is no evidence anyone re-cut a Middle East assumption - if they had, the average price target would have moved off $7.88, which it has not since Citi's June cut to $6. The specific mechanism nobody is modelling is that the Ireland migration breaks in-country data-residency for Gulf government and regulated customers, so it is a renewal problem, not a one-quarter slip.
findings.independence: Resumption of hostilities on the last trading day before the print, separate outlet: https://www.ksat.com/news/world/2026/08/31/uae-intercepts-incoming-iranian-drone-and-other-news-from-the-middle-east/ (2026-08-31). The 44% non-Americas revenue figure and the data-loss language are from the company's own filings (10-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1569345/000156934526000015/cxm-20260131.htm and the Q1 10-Q) - the 10-Q is shared with finding 1, so treat that document as one source.

findings.finding: The 13 August 8-K appointing Microsoft's President of Search & AI, Jordi Ribas, states explicitly that there are no related-party arrangements, family relationships or reportable transactions, and seats him on the Nominating & Corporate Governance and Strategy committees - i.e. it is governance, not a Microsoft commercial relationship - while the same filing shows the board's Strategy Committee was converted from ad hoc to standing at the 2026 annual meeting.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline ('Microsoft AI executive joins Sprinklr board') was aggregated everywhere; the negative related-party representation two paragraphs down was not, and the committee assignments were not. If the market had read the filing rather than the headline, the 17 August effective date would not have produced a -2.8% session followed by nine of eleven up days - the tape is still carrying a partnership expectation the document rules out, which management will have to decline to confirm on tomorrow's call. The standing Strategy Committee cuts the other way and is why my high end is positive.
findings.independence: Proxy confirmation that the Strategy Committee became standing at the 2026 annual meeting: https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CXM/def-14a-sprinklr-inc-definitive-proxy-statement-fe64df26078d.html. Overlaps with finding 1 on the theme 'the run-up is not fundamentally sourced' - different document, sized small for that reason.

searched_and_found_nothing: Whether the Ribas appointment carries any Microsoft commercial agreement - the 8-K affirmatively denies related-party or reportable transactions, so this door is closed rather than open

Insider selling as a signal: the only Q3-window Form 4 sale is Scott Jacob (GC) 71,585 shares at a $6.97 weighted average under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-10-15, and the August Form 4s are RSU grants to Ribas (29,850) and Addis (810,372) - routine
A 13D or activist filing: only 13G/13G-As from BlackRock (18,267,788 shares, 13.7%) and Vanguard (10,723,636, 7.26%), both passive
Any evidence of a take-private or strategic process beyond the Strategy Committee becoming standing
Sprinklr careers page req count - https://www.sprinklr.com/careers/jobs/ returns HTTP 404, so no hiring-velocity read
FX as an unmodelled tailwind - DXY was near 101 through late July 2026 and only eased below 100 in August, so no clean Q2 benefit versus the 4 June guide
WARN notices or a new 2026 restructuring beyond the reported ~2.6% March 2026 action and the February 2025 12% cut

A reliable eight-print reaction history: Yahoo's chart endpoint returned internally inconsistent closes for the 2025-09-03, 2025-12-03 and 2026-03-11 print dates and stockanalysis.com's history table only paginates back to 2026-06-23, so I could verify only two reactions and have widened my bands accordingly rather than invent a median
Any updated sell-side price target after mid-August - the $7.88 average appears to be marked against a ~$6.72 price, i.e. stale
Customer-side complaint signal (support forum, app-store review trend) specific to the UAE migration
baseline_tension: There is no skew and no straddle to agree or disagree with - the baseline itself flags the chain as unusable at a 143% ATM spread on 413 total open interest, so 'what is priced' here is inferred from a +22.6% 20-day run-up and nothing else, which is precisely why a positioning-and-plumbing finding can still be live; my findings cut against the run-up rather than with it, and the honest caveat is that on a name with 14-20% short interest and $75m of buyback authorisation still available after the print, the same thin liquidity that makes the run-up uninformative also makes a squeeze on any raise entirely possible, which is why my low/high bands stay wide.
